sections.overview: Pimelodus pohli is a South American long-whiskered catfish described from Brazil’s São Francisco River drainage.
sections.identification: It has a relatively deep body and a long adipose fin. Adults may show dark spots near the front of the back, while smaller fish have rows of small spots along the sides; a dark bar may mark the lower caudal-fin lobe.
sections.habitat: Its documented range is the São Francisco drainage in Brazil; the sources consulted do not establish finer habitat preferences.
sections.diet: A species-specific diet has not been established in the taxonomic sources consulted.
sections.behavior: The original description is taxonomic and provides little information on the species’ behavior.
sections.reproduction: Reproductive details are not provided in the species description; a later population study exists, but its findings are not summarized here without a verified full-text review.
sections.ecology: Its São Francisco distribution distinguishes it from the other three Pimelodus profiles here. P. pintado is associated with the Laguna Merín basin and is densely spotted. P. stewarti occurs in the Tocantins and is a much smaller species. P. tetramerus is known from the Tapajós–Tocantins region and has four dark flank bands.
sections.conservation: The sources consulted do not provide a species-specific conservation assessment.
